consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.source: TradingView last/next release dates, stepped backwards
history.caveat: Dates are ESTIMATED by stepping the measured cadence gap backwards from the vendor's last release date; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. A cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a SCALE for how far this name travels, never as evidence about a particular past date -- TRT was ranked, traded and never reported on exactly this mistake. AND THE SCALE IS BIASED LOW: most estimated dates land on ordinary sessions, so this median is ordinary-session volatility and not event volatility. Treat it as a LOWER BOUND on how far this name m…

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Nasdaq Nordic disclosure feed (issuer's own category; paged back ~12 days, no date query) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: absent from a register that downloaded successfully, so no disclosed net short position at or above the 0.5% public threshold. A real zero -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0, and the join is on the issuer NAME, so a name spelled differently in the register reads as a zero it should not.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. The issuer's own release of 2026-10-07 says the Q3 report is published Monday 19 Oct 2026 at 08:30 CEST, before the 09:00 Stockholm open, with the earnings call at 09:00 CEST (https://mfn.se/a/aira/aira-tidigarelagger-offentliggorandet-av-delarsrapporten-for-tredje-kvartalet-2026 ; https://mfn.se/a/aira/invitation-to-airas-q3-2026-earnings-call). Window: close 2026-10-16 to close 2026-10-19.

evidence.text: Q3 is the last quarter before Aira for Fortnox exists commercially (it opens to all Fortnox customers on 1 Nov; early access began 15 Oct). So the reported ARR is the HubSpot/standalone base off SEK 1.77m, against a SEK ~111m market cap that more than doubled on the Fortnox story; the print cannot validate the story it is priced on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior print: the Q2 report (2026-07-17, ARR 1.8 MSEK) took the stock from 3.55 to 3.40, -4.2% on the day (Yahoo daily bars).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock already fell about 18% from its 10-12 peak after the investor presentation. With no estimates, nobody has published what Q3 ARR should be. If the market were treating Q3 as a non-event, the pre-report fade would have stopped; it was still falling on 10-16 (7.18 to 6.60).
evidence.independence: The Q2 report gives the ARR base (KSEK 1,767) and says the first Aira Connect paying customer was signed in early July: https://storage.mfn.se/235f4e56-c739-42ab-b9e1-4f1649ae481b/aira-interim-report-q2-2026.pdf

evidence.text: Cash was SEK 14.3m at 30 June on a quarterly operating cash burn of SEK 4.1m plus SEK 1.2m of capitalised development, and Q3/Q4 add a paid DI advertorial, an investor event and an eight-city seminar tour. Q3 cash is likely about SEK 9-10m, roughly two quarters of runway, which the release will make visible. The company has said this is 'more than sufficient to carry Aira to profitability'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. No financing has been announced since listing.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q3 cash figure is not public. A doubled share price is when a pre-profit microcap raises money, and the report was brought forward four days. If the market had priced a raise, the stock would trade with a discount around a likely placing price; instead it holds about 60x ARR. Financing is a question, though: money raised would buy the Fortnox go-to-market, so the sign is uncertain and the size is held small.
evidence.independence: The spend corroborating a higher Q3/Q4 burn: the seminar tour (https://mfn.se/a/aira/aira-publicerar-alla-detaljer-om-aira-for-fortnox-och-presenterar-lanseringsturne) and the DI paid content 'Innehåll från Aira Annons', published 2026-10-09 (https://www.di.se/brandstudio/ai-utmanaren-hjalper-fortnox-kunder-att-hitta-nya-affarer-i-den-egna-datan/)

evidence.text: The golden-ticket early-access programme for Aira for Fortnox opened on 15 Oct, four days before the report, so the release and 09:00 call are the first place management can quantify early Fortnox demand (applications, activations). A company in heavy promotion mode is likely to cite such a number if it is flattering.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. The Fortnox announcement itself (2026-09-29) started a run from 3.97 to 8.05 over nine sessions.
evidence.why_not_priced: No demand number has been published: the 10-14 investor presentation gave the TAM and the go-to-market but no counts. A priced demand number would show as a stable or rising price into the report; instead the stock faded 18% after the presentation.
evidence.independence: The company has invested heavily in investor communication around the launch (investor presentation, recording, podcasts, Kalqyl interview): https://mfn.se/a/aira/aira-publicerar-inspelningen-fran-investerarpresentationen-av-aira-for-fortnox

evidence.text: Exit ACMRR of GBP34.0m covers about 76% of the only published FY27 revenue estimate (Progressive GBP44.5m), the same coverage FY26 had going in (GBP29.5m ACMRR vs GBP40.0m outturn, 74%), and the SET Exchange Cloud contract goes live in H1 FY27, so a reiterated FY27 outlook is the likely first guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Outlook reiterations have been sold: Oct 2025 finals said 'confident' in FY26 with no number and fell -7.7% (AJ Bell: -9.1% intraday); Mar 2026 interims kept the full year in line and fell -11.6%; Jul 2026 'in line' update fell -6.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock has fallen from 225p (15 Sep) to 173p with no RNS, against a one-analyst Buy target of 335p and about 10x trailing EBITDA; if the market were pricing a routine FY27 reiteration the 20-day run-up would not be -20% against the AIM All-Share's c.-4%. Coverage is one house broker plus one paid note, so nobody publishes the ACMRR-to-forecast coverage arithmetic. Capped small because the FY27 bar is a single, pre-July, issuer-sponsored estimate.
evidence.independence: Progressive 16 Feb 2026 note (FY27E revenue GBP44.5m): https://beeksgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/BKS-20260216.pdf ; SET win RNS: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/beeks-financial-cloud-group--bks/stock-exchange-of-thailand-exchange-cloud-win/9747171

evidence.text: Net cash fell from GBP6.96m (Jun 2025) to GBP3.29m (Dec 2025) to GBP0.63m (Jun 2026) on upfront Exchange Cloud and capacity capex, so the audited cash-flow statement in the release will show the full capex and free-cash-flow drain the July update only summarised, the line that sank Luceco on a raised-guide day.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated before; the Mar 2026 interims (net cash halved to GBP3.29m, H1 underlying loss) fell -11.6%, and the Jul 2026 update disclosing net cash of GBP0.63m fell -6.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The headline net cash is public, so this is sized small: what is not yet public is the capex total, operating cash conversion and any financing arrangement. On the financing question the money buys revenue-share Exchange Cloud deployments that the company says are already cash-flow positive (Kraken, ASX) and that are corroborated by ACMRR +15%, which is why it is not larger. A placing or facility announced with results would move this either way.

evidence.text: The shares fell from 225p on 15 Sep to 173.22p at the 16 Oct seal (20-day -20.4%) with no RNS between the 1 Sep SET win and the 7 Oct Notice of Results, against an AIM All-Share index that went from 783 to 771 over the same span, and with no disclosed short.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of a comparable unexplained pre-results slide in the baseline history.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sized 0 on purpose: an unexplained drawdown is worth nothing until a cause is found, and in a $144k/day AIM name the filing record is not the information set (a fund seller would look identical to informed selling). It is filed because it sets both sides of the reaction: a reiterated outlook against an oversold tape, or confirmation of whatever the sellers know.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measurable reaction: the stock closed 210p on 29 Jul and 202p on 30 Jul, within its usual range.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public and 2.5 months old, and it looks like an exercise-and-sell rather than a view. Kept as a near-zero finding because it is the only insider signal and it is a sale, not a buy, into a 20% drawdown.

consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: absent from a register that downloaded successfully, so no disclosed net short position at or above the 0.5% public threshold. A real zero -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0, and the join is on the issuer NAME, so a name spelled differently in the register reads as a zero it should not.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.
